name: Risankizumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 12 weeks (psoriasis) or every 8 weeks via on-body injector (IBD) after IV induction for IBD

discovery.note: Humanised IgG1 antibody against the p19 subunit of IL-23, with Fc mutations reducing effector function; licensed to AbbVie in 2016.

tagline: IL-23 p19 antibody for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease and UC
summary: Risankizumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody that selectively blocks interleukin-23 by binding its p19 subunit. It is used for plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, and has become one of AbbVie's leading immunology products.
mechanism: Risankizumab binds IL-23 p19 and prevents IL-23 from engaging its receptor, without affecting IL-12, which shares only the p40 subunit.

Blocking IL-23 reduces the survival and expansion of pathogenic Th17 and other IL-17- and IL-22-producing cells in skin and gut, producing high and durable rates of skin clearance and mucosal healing.

history.title: AbbVie licence
history.detail: AbbVie licenses risankizumab from Boehringer Ingelheim.

history.title: First approvals
history.detail: Approved in Japan (March), the US and EU (April) for plaque psoriasis.

history.title: IMMerge
history.detail: Risankizumab outperforms secukinumab in psoriasis at week 52.

history.title: PsA and Crohn's disease
history.detail: Approved for psoriatic arthritis (January) and Crohn's disease (June).

history.title: Ulcerative colitis
history.detail: Approved for ulcerative colitis in June.

history.title: SEQUENCE
history.detail: Risankizumab is superior to ustekinumab for endoscopic remission in Crohn's disease.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Liver tests are monitored during IBD induction because of reports of drug-induced liver injury.
Psoriasis maintenance dosing is once every 12 weeks.
